why: The student copies the array one element at a time in a loop, which is the right approach, but the code has two faults: i <= data2.length goes one index too far and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException, and copy is never created with new int[data2.length].

concepts.why: The answer makes no claim about int itself.
It treats data2.length as the last valid index, but the last valid index is data2.length-1.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i <= data2.length; i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: The init, test, update and body are all well formed, but the test allows one pass too many.
i++ is only the standard loop update, and the answer makes no claim about it.
Copying element by element is correct, but no new array is created and the bound goes past the end.
Using <= instead of < with the array length is the OffByOneBound wrong rule.
The answer makes no claim about primitive types.
It treats < and <= as interchangeable, so the loop runs length+1 times.
The answer does not mention aliasing.
